accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurately bounded: asynchronous acceptance/status, publisher versus consumer acknowledgement, transactional duplicate protection, transient/persistent retry handling, per-entity ordering, finite capacity, consumer-group logs and synchronous fit. Live sources support critical claims and external effects are expressly excluded from universal exactly-once claims.

evidence.quote: It does not make an external email or payment atomic, or turn delivery into a universal exactly-once guarantee.

mechanisms.reason: Every failure has actors and state transitions: publish/confirm/work/ack, commit-before-crash redelivery, uniquely constrained transaction, retry isolation, late overwrite, arrival-minus-completion backlog, and per-group offsets. Diagrams show acknowledgement direction and separate group positions consistently.

evidence.quote: Trace publish → broker acceptance → worker effect → consumer acknowledgement. The client observes completion through status.

coherence.reason: Declared HTTP, transaction/uniqueness and arithmetic prerequisites suffice. The first six cards build job lifecycle and failure/capacity reasoning; the queue/log distinction then supports final fit. Per-card dependencies introduce no unexplained required mechanism.

evidence.quote: Choose the request boundary from what the caller needs next, then own the deferred work until completion or visible failure.

decisions.reason: Teaches when work may defer, when access decisions must block, bounded retry versus quarantine, serial per-entity cost, downstream-safe concurrency and producer rejection, and independent replay versus competing work. Costs and failure visibility remain explicit.

evidence.quote: More workers help when workers are the bottleneck and downstream services have spare capacity.

clarity.reason: Names roles, acknowledgement boundaries, stable IDs, idempotency, backpressure, partitions and offsets in context. Examples explain numeric backlog and overtaking without unnecessary story continuity. Assigned diagrams/shared UI assets inspected rather than rendered.

evidence.quote: Committing an offset records progress; it does not delete the event.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria supported: API/broker/worker trace, confirmed durable handoff before acceptance, saved file and status before acknowledgement, pending/ready/failed observation, synchronous access decision and concrete status-operating cost.

All five criteria supported: unacked committed effect can redeliver; early ack can lose work; stable business ID and durable unique transaction make repeats no-ops without exactly-once delivery claim.

Numeric schedule is unnecessary to satisfy finite-budget principle.
All five criteria supported: second write 2 then first 5, delivery versus completion, per-item serial effects including retries, concurrent different items, hot-item throughput cost.

All six criteria supported: 40 jobs/s growth, rising age threatens completion promise, bounded saturated-store concurrency, visible producer control, finite retention/storage, and conditional worker scaling.

All six criteria supported: divided competing work versus independent groups, per-partition group offsets and shared intra-group assignment, progress without deletion, replay conditional on retained required records, partition-scoped order and no universal external-effect guarantee.

sourceChecks.claim: Microsoft asynchronous request-reply explicitly separates 202 acceptance, polling and completed resource; status schema includes pending/running/succeeded/failed. This supports observable delayed completion.

RabbitMQ confirms guide says publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements are orthogonal; each covers its own communication boundary. Manual unacknowledged work is requeued on consumer failure; broker acceptance is not result completion.

AWS idempotent APIs checked live in this batch requires stable caller-operation identifier and ACID coordination of token and effect; RabbitMQ requeue semantics explains repeat delivery. Transaction scope does not include arbitrary external payment/email.

Microsoft retry strategies distinguish transient delayed retry from cancellation of persistent failure; competing-consumers poison-message guidance adds finite delivery-count dead-letter isolation and later investigation.

Microsoft competing-consumers ordering guidance warns receive ordering and dependency constraints and points to per-session single-consumer ordering. The two-worker old/new example directly demonstrates why serial effects including retries are necessary.

Microsoft load-leveling considerations explicitly bound aggregate downstream rate, describe growing queue when producer rate exceeds consumer rate, producer shedding and finite quotas/retention. Arithmetic 100-70 and learner 120-80 are correct.

Kafka 4.1 design describes ordered partitions, one consumer per subscribed group partition, offset checkpoint/rewind and retention independent of consumed position. External output needs coordinated offset/effect state; partitions alone do not grant global exactly-once effects.

Microsoft asynchronous request-reply is for decoupled long-running work with eventual status; dependent access cannot proceed before its necessary decision. Broker/worker/status/retry operation are concrete added responsibilities supported across the cited stack.
